messages:
jane: P2 from ACME — their Dedicated pool is getting 429s starting ~09:05 UTC. They say all traffic should hit pool `dedicated-acme-1` but traces show a mix and most requests dropped with throttle error. customer request_id=rc_20260317_9Xf, model=meta-llama-43b, region=us-west-2. Repro steps in their note below.

ops-bot: Incident alert: high 429 rate on pool dedicated-acme-1 between 2026-03-17T09:05:00Z and 2026-03-17T09:28:00Z. Router fallback engaged.

jane: Repro from their curl: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" -d '{"model":"meta-llama-43b","input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?pool=dedicated-acme-1 -v` -> got 429 with header `x-rw-pool: default-throttle-pool`.

sam: looking. Can you paste the routing policy they should match (or the route tags they set on the pool)? Also need a couple sample request headers.

jane: Their pool tags: `team:acme`, `tier:gold` (set via console). Their routing policy (customer-managed) expects `tier:gold` to go to dedicated pool. I pulled an internal trace for rc_20260317_9Xf: `controlplane: route eval -> tags matched: team:acme ; tier:gold? false -> fallback -> default-throttle-pool`

eli: hmm. I see a routing-eval log snippet from the control-plane: `evaluated tags: ["team:acme","tier: gold"]` (notice the space after colon). Our comparator does exact string match against policy key/value pairs (we store policy as `tier:gold`). If control-plane normalizes tags with a space, match fails.

drew: that would explain why dedicated pool isn't selected. How did tags get that format? UI or agent?

jane: Customer said they used the console tag editor — likely pasted `tier: gold` with a space. We should tolerate that. Customer expects console tags to be equivalent.

sam: Agreed. Two immediate actions: 1) hotfix control-plane routing comparator to trim whitespace for tag keys/values, 2) add a one-off repair to re-evaluate pool metadata for active customers so ACME's pool routes back to dedicated. Which do we prefer first?

eli: Hotfix first (code change) + a config job to reindex tags. I can push a trimmed-compare patch to staging now; if green, promote to prod.

kevin: FYI this is why we had fallback-to-default throttle earlier in Q4 too — might be same class of bug when tag editors insert extra whitespace. Recommend short-term: run a backfill to normalize any tag with `\s` around `:`.

sam: I'll coordinate rollout. ETA: patch to staging in 12 minutes, smoke for 10m, deploy to prod 30m after if OK.

jane: Customer update posted: "We're seeing intermittent 429s, any ETA?" I told them we're investigating and will apply a targeted fix shortly.

ops-bot: Deploy-job started: patch/controlplane-trim-tags to staging at 2026-03-17T09:35:40Z.

eli: Patch applied to staging, running routing-eval unit tests and a small integration with a pool that has `tier: gold` and policy `tier:gold`. Tests show match now succeeds.

sam: Promoting to prod now (canary to 3% routing plane first). Rolling out config backfill job to normalize existing pool tags.

drew: Backfill started; 240 pools queued, ACME pool processed at 09:50:12Z — tag normalized from `tier: gold` -> `tier:gold`.

ops-bot: Canary metrics: 3% canary shows 0 -> 429 errors for matched pools. Full prod at 09:56Z.

jane: ACME confirms at 09:58 UTC they're no longer seeing 429s and all traffic routed to `dedicated-acme-1`. Customer marked as unblocked. :thumbsup:

sam: Root cause summary for postmortem: control-plane routing comparator required exact match and did not trim whitespace around tag key/values. Consequence: pools with tags containing incidental spaces fell through to fallback pool and experienced throttling. Fix: comparator now trims/normalizes tags; backfilled existing pool metadata; added unit/integration tests; console tag editor will also validate/normalize input.

kevin: filing follow-up doc and rolling the postmortem template into incidents. @jane can you paste the customer timeline and final confirmation so we can close P2?

jane: Posted final customer note, closing the loop. Thanks all.
